Quenya: High Elven tongue — Latinate cadence, formal register
Sindarin: Grey Elven tongue — Welsh-influenced phonology, vernacular register
Eucatastrophe: The sudden joyous turn — structural inverse of tragedy
Sub-creation: The human capacity for making that reflects divine creation; the ontology of fantasy
Eä: The world that is; the cosmos created by Eru Ilúvatar
Ainulindalë: The Music of the Ainur — creation myth via song
Valar: The guardian powers who shaped Middle-earth
Maiar: Lesser spirits; Gandalf and Sauron are both Maiar
Silmarils: Three jewels that contained the last light of the Two Trees
Longing: The chief affective register of Tolkien's Elvish prose — untranslatable, close to sehnsucht
Feanorian: Of Fëanor — the tragic type of sub-creator who seeks possession
Scouring: The return-arc pattern where heroes must redeem the home they left
Providence: The invisible moral mechanism that operates through unexpected mercy
Shire-register: Plain, Anglo-Saxon, intimate — the register of home
Rohirric: The language of Rohan; Old English proxy
Black Speech: Sauron's language — privative, harsh, artificially constructed to resist translation
Tengwar: The script devised by Fëanor; meta-linguistic artifact
Deep Time: The affective sense that the present is shallow against immense past
Privation: Evil understood as absence-of-good rather than competing-force
